The True Cost of Dental Implants in London (2025 Guide)

Written By

Dental Implants Team

Navigating the financial landscape of dental implantology can be confusing. Prices vary wildly from £900 to £4,000 per tooth. Why the difference? And what should you realistically budget for?

Transparency is one of our core values. In this guide, we break down the costs so you know exactly what you are paying for.

The Three Parts of an Implant

When comparing quotes, ensure you are comparing like for like. A complete tooth replacement consists of:

  • 1. The Implant Fixture: The titanium screw in the bone.
  • 2. The Abutment: The connector piece.
  • 3. The Crown: The visible porcelain tooth.

Some clinics advertise a low price (e.g., £899) but this is only for the screw. The crown and abutment are added later, doubling the bill. Our price of from £2,950 includes all three components.

Additional Costs to Consider

Depending on complexity, you may need:

  • Consultation & CT Scan: Essential for planning (from ~£95).
  • Extraction: If the failing tooth is still present (from ~£150).
  • Bone Grafting: If bone has been lost (from ~£300).
  • Sedation: For nervous patients (from ~£300).

Why Prices Vary

Higher prices usually reflect:

  • Expertise: Highly experienced implant dentists vs. general dentists.
  • Materials: Premium implant brands with manufacturer guarantees vs. generic clones.
  • Lab Quality: Hand-finished Zirconia crowns vs. mass-produced standard crowns.
  • Location: Central London clinics have higher overheads, but often attract experienced practitioners.

Financing Your Smile

We offer 0% finance plans (subject to status) to spread the cost over 12-24 months, making implants more affordable than a daily coffee. Investing in your smile is investing in your long-term health and confidence.
